comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Killington and Pico on one map (one Ikon destination, Killington-Pico, one ticket; the README's rule for several mountains, as Sun Valley's Bald and Dollar), as resorts.json lists them: way/1228774360 (Killington Resort, 12.8 km2: Killington Peak, Skye Peak, Bear Mountain, Sunrise, Snowdon, Ramshead and the Skyeship base on US 4) and way/1094586461 (Pico Mountain Resort, 2.3 km2), 1.8 km apart at their nearest points, with no lift or trail between them (the resort's Killington/Pico Interconnect is an uphill route). No other ski area lies in the box or the Overpass window. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-12. Killington: its 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf; its labels are outlines with no text layer, so it was rendered at two to four times its size and read tile by tile; rated with the green circle, blue square, black diamond and two black diamonds, with orange terrain-park features and hatching) and its lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status: 19 lifts and 167 alpine trails rated green, blue, black or double black, 8 terrain parks, 5 uphill routes). Pico: its 2026-27 winter trail map (picomountain.com/winter-trail-map, PicoWinterTrailMap2627.pdf, the James Niehues painting, rendered at three to six times its size; blue and black lines with the diamonds) and its lifts and trails status page (picomountain.com/lifts-and-trails-status: 7 lifts and 60 trails, rated the same way). OSM's easy, intermediate, advanced and expert are green, blue, black and double black. Where the map and the status page both rate a run they agree, and they win over OSM (where they differ, the harder stands); where OSM splits a run the map draws in sections (A Slope, Ridge Run, Ovation, Conclusion, Needle's Eye, East Fall, Great Northern, Gold Rush, Giant Killer, K.A.), OSM's pieces already carry the sections' ratings. Ratings: Catwalk - Upper to expert; High Traverse, the first 318 m of Killington's Home Run, Nivis Walk and a 60 m piece of Pipe Dream to intermediate; the top 46 m of Dream Maker Headwall to advanced; a 131 m stretch of Great Eastern to easy; The Stash's gladed line (advanced) to intermediate; at Pico A Slope Cutoff, That A Way (two ways), Upper Sunset 71 and Mid Pike Glades (its line and its outline) to intermediate, and Peekaboo to advanced. Kept as OSM has them: the 165 m connector of Bittersweet to High Road, which the map draws black with a diamond (the status page rates Bittersweet's upper and lower parts blue; the harder stands); Downdraft, one expert way where the status page rates its upper part black; and Bear Trax, one 1.7 km easy way from below Killington Peak to Bear Mountain, whose upper part, from the peak past Helter Skelter, the map draws blue and the status page rates blue (Bear Trax - Upper) while the rest is green on both: OSM does not split the way there (only an 88 m top piece from Blue Heaven is intermediate), so it stays green as most of its length is (an OSM gap; a judgment call); likewise Northbrook Trail (one easy way, labelled green on the map; the status page rates its upper part blue). Parks: The Stash (both its lines), Lil' Stash and Timberline, which the map draws as terrain parks along their whole length, get the park flag. Not flagged: the parks the status page lists on trails of the same name (Easy Street Park, Mouse Run Park, Reason Park, Full House Park and Dream Maker's park), which OSM maps as the whole trail, so a park flag would draw the whole run as a park; and the orange lanes Pico's map draws beside Prospector and Panhandler, which Pico's list does not name as parks. Names from the maps and the status pages: Snowshed Crossover (OSM Northbrook Crossover, the crossover's lower part), Treezy (OSM Treezy Zone), Summit Glade East and West (OSM Summit Glades East and West), Mid K.A. (OSM Middle K.A., two ways), Mid Pike Glades for the glade outline OSM names Middle Pike Glade; lifts Superstar Six (OSM Superstar Express Six), Snowdon Quad (OSM Snowdon Triple), Snowdon Six Express (OSM Snowdon Six), Learn To Carpet (OSM Learn To Snowboard Carpet) and Progression Carpet I (OSM Snowplay Carpet I). Names that differ from the map or the status page only by a space, an apostrophe, a hyphen or a section suffix stay as OSM has them (Sundog for Sun Dog, Stash Way for STASHWAY, The North Way for The Northway, Skye Hawk for SKYEHAWK, Fool's Gold for Fools Gold, Forty Niner for Forty-Niner, Edgemont/Whiffletree for Edgemont / Whiffletree, Superpipe for Superpipe Trail, Learn To Ski And Ride Area for the map's LEARN TO AREA); runs OSM names that neither source prints stay (Low Traverse, Magic Snow Play Park at the Ramshead base, C Slope at Pico, which the map draws blue and the status page omits). No lift name repeats between Killington and Pico, so none takes its mountain's name. Hidden: Snowplay Carpet II (the map draws one carpet in that learning area), the Alpine Training Venue Poma (a race-training lift on neither source), the abandoned Devil's Fiddle and Northeast Passage chairs, a 35 m gondola stub inside the K-1 base station, Pico's Outpost Double (grey on the 2026-27 map, replaced by the Outpost Rope Tow) and the Bonanza Double and Bonanza Rope Tow (replaced by Bonanza Carpet I and II), and the closed glade outlines of Upper Pike Glade, Poma Woods and Doozie (natural=wood without area=yes; their lines stay). Out of bounds: 15 freeride lines outside Killington's polygon, where neither the map nor the status page has a trail, which OSM rates freeride with no backcountry tag: the former Northeast Passage area's Old Sundog, Old Sunrise Trail, Old Gold Dust, Gold Dust (upper and lower), Hawkeye, Nor'easter (two) and Thunderball east of Sunrise Village, and Horn, Old Vagabond, Old Swirl, Old Timberline and two unnamed lines over the ridge west of the Ramshead and Snowdon tops. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Killington's Grizzly and Ledgewood Yurt Trail (blue on both sources; OSM also maps Superstar and Downdraft whole where the status page names their sections); Pico's Outlaw (tagged piste:type=yes in OSM, so left out by the type rule, as Solitude's Evergreen Chutes), Upper K.A. Glades, the Outpost Rope Tow and Bonanza Carpets I and II.

overrides.reason: Catwalk - Upper, the top of Catwalk below Killington Peak, has two black diamonds on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Catwalk - Upper double black; OSM rates it advanced. The resort's sources agree and win.

High Traverse, from the top of the North Ridge Quad across to Bear Trax, is a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and blue in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM rates it easy. The resort's sources agree and win.

The first 318 m of Killington's Home Run, from Bear Trax across Cascade to Great Northern, is drawn blue with a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Home Run blue; OSM rates this piece easy (its other pieces intermediate). The resort's sources agree and win.

Nivis Walk, below the South Ridge Quad's top, is a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and blue in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM rates it advanced. The resort's sources agree and win.

The top 46 m of Dream Maker Headwall, from Great Eastern, is part of the headwall that Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels DREAM MAKER - HEADWALL with one black diamond, and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Dream Maker - Headwall black; OSM rates this piece intermediate (the rest of the headwall advanced). The resort's sources agree and win.

A 60 m piece of Pipe Dream at the South Ridge Link junction: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws Pipe Dream blue along its whole length and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates its upper and lower parts blue; OSM rates this piece easy (the rest intermediate). The resort's sources agree and win.

A 131 m stretch of Great Eastern above the Skyeship base, a second line beside the main way: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws Great Eastern green from Skye Peak to the Skyeship base and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates its upper and lower parts green; OSM rates this stretch intermediate. The resort's sources agree and win.

The Stash, Killington's terrain park in the woods off Skye Peak, is labelled THE STASH twice with blue squares and drawn with terrain-park features along both its lines on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf); the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists The Stash as a blue trail and as a terrain park (S, M, L). OSM rates this line advanced and gladed with no park tag. The resort's sources win: blue, and the park flag.

The Stash, Killington's terrain park in the woods off Skye Peak, drawn with terrain-park features on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and listed as a terrain park (S, M, L) in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM has it as a blue run with no park tag.

Lil' Stash, the small terrain park at the Ramshead base, labelled LIL STASH with a terrain-park feature on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and listed only as a terrain park (XS, S, M) in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM has it as a green run with no park tag.

Timberline on Ramshead is drawn with the terrain-park hatching along its whole length and terrain-park features on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Timberline Park (S, M, L) beside the Timberline trail; OSM has it as a blue run with no park tag.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels this green line, from Great Eastern to the bottom of the Skyeship Express Gondola's second stage, SNOWSHED CROSSOVER (the lower part of the crossover from Bear Mountain), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Snowshed Crossover and no Northbrook Crossover; OSM names it Northbrook Crossover.

This one keeps its numeral as the map's carpet.
